lessons.name: MalocherBot
lessons.summary: MalocherBot is a modular industrial automation cell that combines a robot, controller, task modules, and operator software.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

MalocherBot is a modular industrial automation cell that combines a robot, controller, task modules, and operator software.

![MalocherBot palletizing cell with robot and pallet stations](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-malocherbot.webp)
*MalocherBot palletizing cell with robot and pallet stations. Source: [Unchained Robotics](https://unchainedrobotics.de/en/products/turnkey-solutions/unchained-robotics-malocherbot-palettieren), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Think beyond the arm:** Unchained Robotics packages the surrounding equipment into a usable production station rather than selling only a moving mechanism.
- **A concrete task is palletizing:** the robot takes boxes and builds a planned stack on a shipping pallet.
- **Software analogy:** its Base Unit resembles a server with plug-in services; LUNA connects the robot and selected task modules behind one interface.

> **Key idea:** A useful industrial robot is a coordinated system, not just an arm with a successful motion demo.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **The Base Unit contains** the robot, robot controller, system computer, and LUNA software.
- **Palletizer modules attach** to the Base Unit, which recognizes and configures them; the operator supplies box dimensions, weights, and stack patterns.
- **Worked calculation:** the advertised ceiling of 12 packages per minute corresponds to 60 ÷ 12 = 5 seconds per package, not guaranteed production performance.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Example configuration** | MalocherBot Palletizing |
| **Maximum box weight** | 20 kg |
| **Advertised maximum rate** | 12 packages/minute |
| **Maximum stack height** | 1.8 m |
| **Palletizer modules** | 1 or 2 |

## Key terms

- **Cell**: a robot and the surrounding equipment that perform one production task.
- **Palletizing**: arranging packages in layers on a pallet.
- **Turnkey**: supplied as an integrated solution rather than separate components.
- **Controller**: the computer responsible for executing robot motion.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch the maker’s cell video and identify the Base Unit and pallet positions.
2. **Write a mock job description:** box dimensions, mass, pallet pattern, and what should happen when a pallet is full.
3. **Request a configured quote** before planning hardware access; the complete student deployment cost is unknown.

## Used in

- **Builder: Unchained Robotics.** compare the machine-tending and picking variants to see how the same integration idea serves different processes.
- **Study the boundaries:** a working box-stacking example does not automatically solve arbitrary-object grasping.

lessons.name: MORFOSE
lessons.summary: MORFOSE is a modular industrial robot whose rotating modules can be rearranged to suit different manufacturing tasks.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

MORFOSE is a modular industrial robot whose rotating modules can be rearranged to suit different manufacturing tasks.

![MORFOSE rotating modules and tool flange](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-morfose.webp)
*MORFOSE rotating modules and tool flange. Source: [MS-Innov](https://www.ms-innov.fr/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/COMMERCIAL_BOOKLET_MORFOSE.pdf), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Mechanics changes the program:** rebuilding the arm changes where its tool can move, not merely its appearance.
- **MS-Innov developed MORFOSE:** the manufacturer presents handling, assembly, inspection, and material-processing uses.
- **Software analogy:** reusable modules resemble software components, but their arrangement changes the physical geometry that the motion controller must understand.

> **Key idea:** Mechanical modularity is useful only when the controller and task configuration agree with the actual assembled robot.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Reconfigurable connections** let an operator replace modules or change the arm arrangement.
- **Unlimited axis rotation** means the published design has no rotational end stop on each module; it does not mean unlimited load capacity.
- **MARCUS software** provides graphical programming; the brochure also describes remotely synchronized modules for equipment such as turntables.
- **Worked comparison:** a six-axis arm plus a two-axis positioner has six arm axes, not eight axes inside the arm.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Maker’s product-page payload** | Up to 11 kg |
| **Reach** | Up to 1,200 mm |
| **Repeatability** | 0.1 mm |
| **Protection rating** | IP54 |
| **Module replacement/reconfiguration** | Under 10 minutes, maker claim |

## Key terms

- **Axis**: one independently controlled movement.
- **Positioner**: a separate mechanism that turns or positions the workpiece.
- **Repeatability**: how consistently the robot returns to a previously taught position.
- **Reconfiguration**: changing the physical arrangement of modules.

## Getting started

1. **Begin free:** watch the product demonstration and mark which motion belongs to the arm versus external equipment.
2. **Compare sources:** the older brochure advertises up to 27 kg; use the configuration-specific product page rather than mixing those limits.
3. **Sketch one handling task** and request the matching configuration and quote; its current cost is unknown.

## Used in

- **MS-Innov is the map connection:** this robot illustrates its modular approach to industrial automation.
- **Compare with fixed arms:** ask which setup changes require rebuilding hardware and which require only editing the task.

lessons.name: MOTOMAN HC10DTP
lessons.summary: The MOTOMAN HC10DTP is a six-axis collaborative industrial arm with a 10 kg rated payload and hand-guided teaching.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The MOTOMAN HC10DTP is a six-axis collaborative industrial arm with a 10 kg rated payload and hand-guided teaching.

![MOTOMAN HC10DTP articulated collaborative robot](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-motoman-hc10dtp.webp)
*MOTOMAN HC10DTP articulated collaborative robot. Source: [Yaskawa](https://www.yaskawa.eu.com/robotics/robots/collaborative/productdetail/product/hc10dtp_17024), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Industrial scale is tangible:** this is production equipment for handling, not a small desktop learning kit.
- **Yaskawa Electric offers hand guidance:** an operator moves the wrist to teach positions, then the controller replays the programmed task.
- **Software analogy:** teaching points resembles recording function arguments; the controller executes the motion, but tools and surroundings still determine whether the task succeeds.

> **Key idea:** A collaborative arm’s force monitoring is one part of application safety, not permission to ignore the gripper or workpiece.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Six driven axes** position and orient the tool; supply cables are routed through the arm to the wrist.
- **Joint torque sensors** monitor twisting forces, supporting collision detection and the manufacturer’s stop and release functions.
- **Worked reach comparison:** the published absolute reach is 1,379 mm, while effective reach is 1,200 mm; these use different reference points.
- **Direct Teach buttons** save positions at the wrist; either the standard teach pendant or Smart Pendant can also program the robot.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Axes** | 6 |
| **Rated payload** | 10 kg |
| **Absolute reach** | 1,379 mm |
| **Effective reach** | 1,200 mm |
| **Repeatability** | 0.05 mm |
| **Robot weight** | 58 kg |
| **Power supply rating** | 1 kVA |

> **Watch out:** Moving arms, tools, and packages can trap or strike people; collaborative settings must match the complete application.

## Key terms

- **Payload**: the supported load at the tool, subject to the maker’s load conditions.
- **Torque sensor**: a sensor measuring twisting force at a joint.
- **Teach pendant**: a handheld interface for configuring and programming motion.
- **Effective reach**: the reach defined using the maker’s specified working reference points.

## Getting started

1. **Start free with the demonstration:** identify the tool and material flow before examining programming.
2. **Draw a pick-and-place cell:** include approach positions, pallet or fixture, and an explicit stopped state.
3. **Arrange a supplier demonstration:** price and complete cell cost are unknown; do not test contact behavior with your body.

## Used in

- **Yaskawa Electric is the builder:** compare the HC family’s reach and payload before choosing equipment.
- **Application examples matter:** a palletizer adds gripping, package presentation, and stacking logic beyond the arm specification.

lessons.name: NB-120
lessons.summary: NB-120 is Nimbl’Bot’s modular industrial arm prototype for operations such as machining, with many controllable bending sections.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

NB-120 is Nimbl’Bot’s modular industrial arm prototype for operations such as machining, with many controllable bending sections.

![NB-120 prototype with repeated metal modules](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-nb-120.webp)
*NB-120 prototype with repeated metal modules. Source: [Nimbl’Bot](https://nimbl-bot.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Flyer-corporate_Nimbl-Bot_ENG_2022_OK-web.pdf), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Its shape differs from a familiar elbow arm:** repeated modules bend along the length rather than concentrating motion at a few large joints.
- **Nimbl'Bot documents work with CEA:** the use case investigates machining complex materials after unsuitable tests with conventional solutions.
- **Software analogy:** commanding the tool is like specifying an API result while a solver chooses internal module states to produce it.

> **Key idea:** A prototype specification describes a particular configuration; it is not a promise that every modular assembly has the same capabilities.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **The 2022 flyer describes** a steel NB-120 prototype suitable for drilling, routing, and sanding.
- **A hollow structure** provides internal passage for services such as pipes; the flyer shows passages for pipes up to 8 mm diameter.
- **The CEA example** combines a spindle, meaning a rotating machining tool drive, with a CNC interface that accepts G-code motion instructions.
- **Worked comparison:** the flyer’s ten-module example is 2 m long; the current homepage lists a 1,000 mm configuration. Do not merge them.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Historical flyer configuration** | 10 modules |
| **Historical length** | 2 m |
| **Historical payload** | 10 kg |
| **Diameter** | 120 mm |
| **CEA prototype spindle** | 1.5 kW |
| **CEA example workspace** | 1 × 1 × 1 m |

> **Watch out:** A machining spindle introduces cutting and ejected-material hazards beyond those of moving the arm.

## Key terms

- **Module**: a repeatable mechanical unit in the arm.
- **Redundancy**: having more internal motion choices than a tool task alone requires.
- **G-code**: instructions describing manufacturing-machine movements.
- **Spindle**: the rotating drive carrying a machining tool.

## Getting started

1. **Begin free:** watch the maker’s NB-120 simulation and separate simulated motion from demonstrated hardware performance.
2. **Read the flyer and CEA page together:** label each number with its source and configuration.
3. **Draft a tool-path experiment** without cutting material; current purchase access, supported software, and price are unknown.

## Used in

- **Nimbl'Bot is the builder:** its NB-55 targets narrower inspection environments rather than simply being the same arm at another scale.
- **CEA machining is the documented use case:** treat it as development evidence, not a general accuracy benchmark.

lessons.name: NB-55
lessons.summary: NB-55 is Nimbl’Bot’s slender modular arm for inspection and intervention in confined spaces.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

NB-55 is Nimbl’Bot’s slender modular arm for inspection and intervention in confined spaces.

![NB-55 prototype bent into a tight curve](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-nb-55.webp)
*NB-55 prototype bent into a tight curve. Source: [Nimbl’Bot](https://nimbl-bot.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Flyer-corporate_Nimbl-Bot_ENG_2022_OK-web.pdf), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Access is the central problem:** the robot is intended to reach areas that are difficult or risky for a person to inspect.
- **The maker describes rover mounting:** mobility brings the arm to the site, while the arm threads the tool into the inspection area.
- **Software analogy:** tool-path planning resembles routing around obstacles, except the entire physical arm must fit, not just its endpoint.

> **Key idea:** Reaching the target is insufficient if an intermediate arm section collides with the environment.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Repeated bending modules** make a snake-like shape; a hollow interior can carry communication cables and a 12 V supply in the historical design.
- **The 2022 flyer** lists NB-55 as a functional prototype for inspection and intervention, with a 60 mm diameter and 10 cm bending radius.
- **Configuration matters:** the same flyer describes an 80 cm prototype and a separate ten-module example measuring 60 cm.
- **Worked comparison:** that ten-module example has a stated 300° working area; it does not imply every point along a pipe is reachable.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **2022 prototype diameter** | 60 mm |
| **2022 listed length** | 80 cm |
| **2022 bending radius** | 10 cm |
| **2022 payload capacity** | 1 kg |
| **Ten-module example length** | 60 cm |
| **Ten-module working area** | 300° |

## Key terms

- **Bending radius**: the radius of the curve a bending section makes.
- **Confined space**: a restricted environment with limited room for access and movement.
- **Rover**: a mobile base carrying equipment.
- **Tool path**: the sequence of positions followed by the working end.

## Getting started

1. **Start free with the agility video:** track both the tip and the middle sections as the arm moves.
2. **Compare the dated flyer with the homepage:** the latter introduces NB K7-60 as a newer generation; do not copy its specifications into NB-55.
3. **Sketch a pipe-inspection scene** and identify pinch points and cable routing; present access and cost are unknown.

## Used in

- **Nimbl'Bot is the map connection:** NB-55 illustrates inspection-oriented manipulation.
- **Contrast NB-120:** the larger machining prototype solves a different tooling problem, even though both use modular construction.

lessons.name: Ned2
lessons.summary: Ned2 is Niryo’s six-axis desktop robot arm for learning programming and small-object manipulation.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Ned2 is Niryo’s six-axis desktop robot arm for learning programming and small-object manipulation.

![Ned2 desktop educational robot in a teaching setup](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-ned2.webp)
*Ned2 desktop educational robot in a teaching setup. Source: [Niryo](https://niryo.com/6-axis-educative-robot-ned2/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A complete teaching platform** lets software students study moving hardware without first designing an arm.
- **Niryo offers graphical and code-based programming:** its technical sheet lists Niryo Studio, the Niryo API, and ROS.
- **Software analogy:** a robot API turns a desired operation into physical effects; unlike a pure function, a failed grasp changes the next input scene.

> **Key idea:** A repeatable arm still needs correctly placed objects, a suitable tool, and a task that fits its small payload.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Six rotating joints** position and orient the end tool; the structure uses aluminum, ABS plastic, and steel.
- **Digital and analog connections** link peripherals, while dedicated interfaces support a gripper, vacuum pump, and conveyor.
- **The 2025 technical sheet** specifies 300 g payload at its stated 20 mm tool-center condition; load placement therefore matters.
- **Worked calculation:** 300 g equals 0.3 kg, so this is a small-object platform rather than an industrial carton-handling arm.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Rotating joints** | 6 |
| **Robot mass** | 7 kg |
| **Payload** | 300 g, specified at z = 20 mm TCP |
| **Reach** | 490 mm |
| **Repeatability** | ±0.5 mm, ISO 9283 |
| **Average standard-use power** | 20 W |

## Key terms

- **TCP**: tool center point: the reference point used to describe tool motion.
- **Repeatability**: consistency when returning to the same commanded position.
- **Peripheral**: an attached device such as a gripper or conveyor.
- **API**: a documented interface through which a program requests robot operations.

## Getting started

1. **Start free with Niryo Academy:** follow the Ned2 getting-started course and identify the robot’s basic controls.
2. **On an available arm,** begin with the official setup and calibration workflow before a simple empty-gripper movement.
3. **Build a small pick-and-place exercise** with known object positions; purchase price and complete classroom setup cost are unknown.

## Used in

- **Niryo is the builder:** Ned2 is its educational arm in this map.
- **Read the stack’s version labels:** the linked documentation explicitly covers Ned2 and Ned3pro, so select the Ned2 instructions rather than assuming identical hardware.

lessons.name: OMX
lessons.summary: OMX is ROBOTIS’s lightweight leader–follower arm platform for teleoperation and imitation-learning experiments.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

OMX is ROBOTIS’s lightweight leader–follower arm platform for teleoperation and imitation-learning experiments.

![OMX leader–follower manipulation hardware](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-omx.webp)
*OMX leader–follower manipulation hardware. Source: [ROBOTIS](https://ai.robotis.com/omx/hardware_omx.html), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Demonstrations become data:** move the leader and the follower performs the corresponding motion.
- **ROBOTIS uses DYNAMIXEL-X actuators** and ROS 2 workflows, with documented integration into LeRobot.
- **Software analogy:** the leader is an input device, while the follower is a physical output device; recording both makes a dataset rather than just a remote-control session.

> **Key idea:** A leader–follower system produces useful training data only when its physical setup and recorded observations agree.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **OMX-L is the leader:** its lightweight mechanism provides the human input; OMX-F is the powered follower.
- **Each has five arm joints plus a gripper:** the gripper’s opening is not an extra arm-orientation axis.
- **Follower load depends on reach:** the maker lists 100 g at full extension and 250 g at normal reach.
- **Worked calculation:** 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5; the normal-reach payload is 2.5 times the full-reach figure, not a universal lifting limit.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Arm layout** | 5 joints + gripper per unit |
| **Follower reach** | 400 mm |
| **Follower mass** | 560 g |
| **Follower supply** | 12 VDC |
| **Leader supply** | 5 VDC |
| **Full-reach payload** | 100 g |
| **Normal-reach payload** | 250 g |

## Key terms

- **Leader**: the mechanism a person moves to issue commands.
- **Follower**: the robot executing those commands.
- **Imitation learning**: learning robot behavior from recorded demonstrations.
- **Homing**: moving into the documented reference state before operation.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch the OMX introduction and read the cable and setup instructions.
2. **Check the two supply voltages** and connect each unit exactly as the maker specifies; kit cost is unknown.
3. **Follow setup and operation guides** before collecting a simple object-transfer demonstration.

## Used in

- **ROBOTIS builds OMX:** its documented LeRobot workflow makes it a comparison platform for SO-101.
- **Keep evaluation separate from teaching:** record demonstrations first, then test whether a learned behavior works on new object placements.

lessons.name: OMY
lessons.summary: OMY is ROBOTIS’s six-joint manipulator family for teleoperation, learned manipulation, and research automation.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

OMY is ROBOTIS’s six-joint manipulator family for teleoperation, learned manipulation, and research automation.

![OMY leader–follower manipulation hardware](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-omy.webp)
*OMY leader–follower manipulation hardware. Source: [ROBOTIS](https://ai.robotis.com/omy/hardware_omy.html), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Human demonstrations connect code to motion:** the OMY-AI3M set pairs an OMY-L100 leader with an OMY-F3M follower.
- **ROBOTIS documents the complete system:** the follower includes a two-finger hand and an Intel RealSense D405 depth camera.
- **Software analogy:** a demonstration is a logged input/output trace; training uses many traces to produce a policy that chooses later robot actions.

> **Key idea:** A leader–follower system produces useful training data only when its physical setup and recorded observations agree.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **DYNAMIXEL-Y actuators** drive six follower joints; Ethernet connects the host and RS485 carries internal communication.
- **The camera supplies depth observations,** while the hand supplies physical contact; neither alone completes a manipulation task.
- **Six degrees of freedom** describe arm motion, not six independent fingers or autonomous capabilities.
- **Worked comparison:** 580 mm reach is 0.58 m; the 3 kg payload specification does not make OMY a large-pallet robot.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Follower model** | OMY-F3M |
| **Arm degrees of freedom** | 6 |
| **Payload** | 3 kg |
| **Reach** | 580 mm |
| **Follower mass** | 13.5 kg |
| **Supply** | 24 VDC |
| **Repeatability** | ±0.05 mm |

## Key terms

- **Degree of freedom**: an independently controlled movement.
- **Depth camera**: a camera that also estimates distance to visible surfaces.
- **Policy**: a function mapping observations to chosen actions.
- **Inference**: running a trained model to produce outputs.

## Getting started

1. **Begin free:** watch the OMY introduction and compare the available leader and follower configurations.
2. **Read the official setup guide:** confirm the host connection, supplied power equipment, and emergency stop before operation.
3. **Plan a demonstration dataset** for one small-object task; hardware pricing and complete experiment cost are unknown.

## Used in

- **ROBOTIS is the builder:** OMY is a larger research platform than OMX, not merely another name for it.
- **Its documented learning workflow** supports collecting demonstrations and later running models; owning the arm does not itself provide a trained task policy.

lessons.summary: P-Rob is F&P Robotics’ family of collaborative arms; P-Rob Eco is a concrete variant for light handling and automation.

## In one sentence

P-Rob is F&P Robotics’ family of collaborative arms; P-Rob Eco is a concrete variant for light handling and automation.

![P-Rob Eco collaborative robot arm](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-p-rob.webp)
*P-Rob Eco collaborative robot arm. Source: [F&P Robotics](https://www.fp-robotics.com/solutions/cobots/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A named family is not one specification:** choose a particular P-Rob variant before comparing payload or reach.
- **BFH HuCE Robotics Laboratory lists F&P P-Rob** in its robot park, giving this map node a concrete research connection.
- **Software analogy:** an arm is a hardware backend; the task software still needs adapters for the gripper, camera, and surrounding instruments.

> **Key idea:** Compare a complete variant and its integration interfaces, not specifications collected from different generations of the same robot family.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **P-Rob Eco uses six axes:** the vendor listing describes collision detection, a web-based interface, and a compact collaborative arm.
- **The controller executes motion,** while a chosen end tool determines whether the system grips a sample, carries an item, or operates a fixture.
- **The manufacturer’s application page** discusses laboratory handling, electronic testing, and bottle filling rather than claiming one universal task.
- **Worked planning example:** list sample pickup, instrument loading, and return as separate operations; give each an explicit success or failure outcome.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Illustrated variant** | P-Rob Eco |
| **Arm axes** | 6 |
| **Variant payload** | 5 kg |
| **Variant reach** | 900 mm |
| **Programming interface** | myP software / web interface |

## Key terms

- **Cobot**: a robot designed to support collaborative applications, with application-specific safety requirements.
- **End tool**: the device attached to the arm for the actual task.
- **Integration**: connecting the arm, tools, sensing, and task software.
- **Variant**: a particular model within a broader product family.

## Getting started

1. **Begin free:** watch the P-Rob Eco demonstration and identify its arm and gripper.
2. **Inspect the Eco listing** rather than transferring numbers from another P-Rob generation; current complete-system cost is unknown.
3. **Ask BFH about appropriate access:** its equipment-leasing statement concerns SMEs, not automatic student access.

## Used in

- **F&P Robotics is the builder:** the official cobot page provides industrial and laboratory application context.
- **BFH HuCE Robotics Laboratory is the mapped user:** treat that as evidence of a research platform, not proof of an open student hardware program.
